To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amphiphilic molecular isomers with a flexible and rigid segment self-assemble into different supramolecular aggregates by controlling their sequence of the rigid segment.

the self-assembling of molecular isomers with different sequences of the rod segment and the length of PEO chains results in the formation of supramolecular structures in bulk and in water, which is due to the control of the interactions of the rigid rod building blocks.

the self-assembling behaviors of the rod building unit and the length of PEO chains in amphiphilic molecular isomers dramatically affect the supramolecular aggregation in bulk and in an aqueous solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of amphiphilc molecules that are able to self-organise into various supramolecualr aggregates.
the design of supramolecular assemblies by the self-organization of amphiphillic molecular isomers.
the construction of supramolecular assemblies from self-organization of amphiphillic coil-rod-coils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supramolecular aggregates formed in bulk and in solution are determined by a delicate balance between the non-covalently interacting rod building blocks and the flexible chains.
the molecular isomers with different sequences of the rod building units can self-organize in bulk and in solution into various supramolecules, which can be used in various applications.
the supramolecular assemblies can be tuned by the molecular isomers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular structure and the length of a rod building block and a flexible chain play an important role in the self-organization of the amphiphilic molecules.
the supramolecular assembly is determined by the sequence of the building block in the rod and the length of PEO chains.
the molecular structure, especially the sequence of the rigid blocks, plays a critical role for the self-organization of the amphiphilic molecular isomers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supramolecular assemblies can be constructed by the self-organization of molecular isomers.
the molecular design of amphiphilics with a rod building unit and the length of flexible chains are important for the creation of various supramolecular assemblies.
the supramolecular aggregates of the amphiphilic molecular isomers are constructed through the noncovalent interactions between the rigid rod blocks.
